paragraphs.text: Supplementary material
DENT-STRIDE: Domain-Configured Structured FDI Tooth Detection Across Panoramic Radiographs and Intraoral Photographs

Additional component descriptions, complete numerical ablations, comparator protocols, and exploratory visual analyses. Experimental families retain their own configurations; historical outputs are not substituted for final-model predictions.
S1. Optional feature-processing components
The main article shows the Mobile HOOA architecture (Fig. 5). Figs. S1–S3 document comparison refiners that are not required by the three selected recipes: CEDv2, SMWG, MPF, and UCM.

CEDv2 operates on projected features before the main encoder. Coarse features are upsampled and laterally projected to provide sigmoid guidance for the adjacent finer level; aligned branches are concatenated and refined. The bottom-up path fuses learned stride-2 features reciprocally with coarser branches (Fig. S1).

Fig. S1. CEDv2 comparison architecture. Guided top-down and bottom-up operations refine the projected pyramid before the main encoder. This module is not active in any selected recipe. ↑ denotes resizing/upsampling except the labelled learned stride-2 operation; C denotes concatenation, σ sigmoid, and ⊙ element-wise multiplication.

The auxiliary SMWG refiner acts on projected P3/P4/P5 before encoder aggregation. A pre-projection is transformed with rFFT2 into a complex spectrum. Fixed radial low-, mid-, and high-frequency masks are mixed by per-channel softmax weights and applied through the bounded modulation 1 + 0.20 × tanh(M). After irFFT2 and post-projection, a dynamic channel gate computed from the pre-FFT feature controls a residual update with α_s = 0.35 × sigmoid(s). Fine-to-coarse guidance computes a local high-pass residual P−AvgPool3×3(P), resizes and projects it to the next coarser level, predicts a sigmoid guide, and applies depthwise 3×3 refinement with a bounded residual update. The evaluated implementation is Fourier-based and does not perform a discrete wavelet decomposition (Fig. S2).

Fig. S2. SMWG, an optional Fourier spectral-modulation and fine-to-coarse detail-guidance refiner. This evaluated implementation uses rFFT2/irFFT2 with radial frequency-band masks; it does not perform a discrete wavelet decomposition.

After FPN/PAN aggregation, the auxiliary MPF and UCM refiners can be applied independently to each output level. MPF combines a depthwise 5×5 local-spatial branch, a global-average-pooled channel-reweighting branch, and a 1×1→3×3 context branch using three softmax-normalized weights; the mixture is injected with α_m=0.35×sigmoid(s). UCM computes μ=AvgPool₅×₅(x) and v=ReLU[AvgPool₅×₅(x²)−μ²]. A learned uncertainty map U interpolates a depthwise detail update D from x−μ and a projected context update C from μ, yielding R=U⊙D+(1−U)⊙C and P_ucm=x+α_uR with α_u=0.35×sigmoid(s). Fig. S3 reflects this per-level refinement view, and when both are enabled MPF precedes UCM on each level.

Fig. S3. MPF and UCM per-level comparison refiners. MPF mixes local, channel-reweighting, and context paths; UCM uses local mean/variance to interpolate detail and context updates. MPF precedes UCM when both are enabled.
S2. Complete recipe and inter-module results

Table S1 contains non-selected cohort-specific recipes. Module labels alone do not define a matched comparison because training settings differ across families. Selected models and local references remain in main Table 3. Table S2 is the separate, fixed-recipe 16-way feature experiment visualized in main Fig. 7.
Table S1. Historical recipe-level development/validation comparisons.

Metric values are copied from the original manuscript tables, retaining their original precision. “Prototype” is the historical configuration label, not prototype-score fusion. “SpatialShape” is a prior-enabled complete recipe, not a same-checkpoint toggle.

For Table S2, DualOpt is active in every row, with a common seed, input policy, training budget, and checkpoint-selection rule. All four-feature combinations are included. The 73.431 AP CMFA + DualOpt result belongs to this historical family and is not the selected 73.115 AP DSLR recipe in main Tables 3–4.
Table S2. Complete four-feature-module ablation on DSLR with DualOpt fixed.

+/− indicate enabled/disabled CMFA, SMWG, UCM, and MPF. Metrics are percentage points and parameters are millions. These are individual-run results, not means across seeds. The main figure displays the same values without smoothing or uncertainty bars.
S3. Progressive identity-mechanism ablation

The eight experiments in Table S3 hold a historical feature stack fixed within each cohort and progressively enable factor auxiliary heads, prototype auxiliary learning, and the geometric prior. The common stack contains CMFA, HOOA, EFRUF, SINF, and SMWG; these are not the smaller final recipes. Factor and prototype inference-fusion weights are zero in this family. Thus, the factor/prototype rows test auxiliary supervision, whereas the final row also adds inference-time geometric/view scoring. All rows belong to the same recorded run family, but each is a single training run; no across-seed variance is estimated.
Table S3. Progressive identity ablation on a fixed historical feature stack.

The bank uses four prototypes per class and temperature 0.20. The approximately 15.5 M-parameter reference is not Local DEIM–D-FINE in main Table 3. This family does not isolate center versus shape or the final Mobile factor-score fusion.

Relative to the factor-only row, prototype auxiliary supervision changes AP by +0.647 on smartphone photographs and +0.174 on DENTEX. Adding the combined geometric prior changes AP by −1.318 and +0.489, respectively. The opposing directions motivate acquisition-specific evaluation and do not establish a universal benefit of spatial scoring.
S4. Upstream baselines, repeated runs, and module migration

Table S4 reports existing upstream baseline training runs with seeds 0, 1, and 2. Mean and sample standard deviation are computed over the three run-specific best validation checkpoints. These are repeated runs of the official implementations, not repeated runs of the final DENT-STRIDE configurations. In particular, their standard deviations must not be attached to the selected AP values in main Table 3.
Table S4. Three-seed official baseline AP.
All entries are validation-selected estimates. Three-seed baseline variability does not remove selection bias or establish uncertainty for a differently configured final model.

The available seed-0 migration experiments also show that a module recipe is not universally beneficial when moved to an upstream implementation. The panoramic factor/prototype/SpatialShape migration increases AP from 53.349 to 54.151; the smartphone DualOpt migration decreases AP from 53.605 to 52.967; and the DSLR CMFA + DualOpt migration decreases AP from 72.557 to 72.095. These are distinct implementation-level comparisons and are not replacements for the final cohort-specific results.
S5. Additional historical cross-framework comparisons

Table S5 restores the available conventional-detector references for DENTEX and smartphone photographs. They retain native framework optimization, pretraining, and post-processing. The archived smartphone comparator annotations and final Mobile annotations have different serialized hashes; therefore these results are shown as historical framework references rather than asserted to be a byte-identical, fully harmonized comparison with the selected 1024-resolution Mobile model. No claim of universal accuracy leadership is drawn from this table.
Table S5. Historical conventional-detector development comparisons.
Framework-native training and output processing are retained. The main manuscript distinguishes the selected-recipe evidence from these development comparisons.
S6. Shape statistics and additional visual analyses

Main Fig. 3 shows the training-derived center templates. Fig. S4 provides complementary width/height statistics; the inference model uses their joint log-shape quadratic score, not independent marginal histograms. Figs. S5–S7 contain historical panoramic/DSLR predictions and prior-switch cases, not predictions from the final selected-checkpoint quantitative evaluations.

Fig. S4. Normalized width and height of 16,234 DENTEX training boxes by FDI class. These distributions describe training geometry; the SpatialShape inference term is a joint quadratic score in log-width/log-height.

Fig. S5. Historical same-image panoramic detector comparison using clinical FDI labels and a common display threshold. The DENT-STRIDE prediction source differs from the selected-checkpoint replay in main Table 5; the examples provide qualitative context only.
Fig. S6. Historical same-image DSLR detector comparison. These archived outputs illustrate comparative error patterns and are not a replay of the selected 73.115 AP checkpoint.

The acquisition/error atlas is presented in main Fig. 1. Fig. S7 expands historical same-checkpoint prior-help/prior-harm examples: correction can alter an FDI assignment in either direction, without estimating benefit/harm frequencies. Fig. S8 shows genuine intermediate tensors from a refiner-enabled model; responses are not causal ablations or clinically validated explanations.

Fig. S7. Historical same-checkpoint prior-help/prior-harm examples. Only anatomical scoring changes within each displayed comparison. This visual checkpoint differs from the selected checkpoint in main Table 5; no numerical result from that table is attributed to these images.

Fig. S8. Exploratory CMFA/HOOA forward-pass responses from DSLR validation image 46 in a refiner-enabled configuration. Channel-gate grids index channels, not anatomy; display normalization is separate from raw gate values. HOOA is absent from the final DSLR recipe. These tensors are not Grad-CAM maps or evidence of an AP gain from every branch.
S7. Evaluation families and visualization methods

Native training-log metrics and FP32 replay metrics are kept as separate evaluation streams. Likewise, local and official DEIM models are separate implementations. Table S6 summarizes the valid interpretation of each family.
Table S6. Evaluation scope of the experimental families.
Quantitative visualization

Main Fig. 6 plots all ten rows of main Table 4 without omitting larger or higher-AP comparators. Main Fig. 7 plots all 16 feature combinations from the original ablation summary in design order. AP is multiplied by 100 where source values are proportions; parameter counts are divided by 10⁶ where recorded as integers. No missing observations, confidence intervals, interpolated curves, or synthetic measurements are introduced. The accompanying CSV files and rebuild_quantitative_figures.py reproduce both plots as PNG, SVG, and PDF.

Python/Matplotlib plotting code was prepared with assistance from ChatGPT (GPT-6 Astra Pro, OpenAI). Source numeric records were retained and checked against the manuscript tables. Existing anatomical/prediction figures were reused; only surrounding whitespace, obsolete panel labels, or the complementary HOOA/CEDv2 panel boundary was cropped. Clinical pixels, predicted boxes, FDI labels, gate values, and anatomical distributions were not retouched or regenerated. Original high-resolution or editable sources should be retained for editorial assessment.
